title.en: Illustrative Cost of a 200 MW AI Training Campus (Table 2) and Appendix A Assumptions
title.zh: 200 MW AI 训练校区示意成本（表2）及附录A成本假设

description.en: Table 2 of the paper: component-level cost and share for a representative 200 MW AI training campus (200 MW total facility power = 166.7 MW critical IT at PUE 1.2; ~1,170 GB300 NVL72 racks at 142 kW/rack), together with the underlying Appendix A assumptions and benchmark comparisons (JLL, Cleanview, Turner & Townsend, Moody's).
description.zh: 论文表2：一个代表性 200 MW AI 训练校区分项成本与占比（200 MW 总设施功率 = PUE 1.2 下 166.7 MW 关键 IT 容量；约 1,170 个 GB300 NVL72 机架、每架 142 kW），并收录附录A的全部成本假设与基准对比（JLL、Cleanview、Turner & Townsend、Moody's）。

sections: Appendix A. Representative AI Campus Cost
II. AI as a Physical Capital Boom

notes: Printed page number = PDF page − 2. Table 2 is on PDF page 21 (printed p.19); Appendix A spans PDF pages 20–22 (printed pp.18–20); Section II cost stack on PDF page 6 (printed p.4).
Table 2 prints costs exactly as 2.200 / 0.400 / 5.616 / 4.680 / 0.468 / 0.234 / 0.234 ($ billions) and total 8.216; JSON numbers drop trailing zeros (e.g. 2.2 for 2.200) with no change in value.

Table 2 notes (verbatim key points): 'The campus has 200 MW of total facility power, equivalent to 166.7 MW of critical IT capacity at a PUE of 1.2. The rack count is interpreted as a cluster-equivalent measure: the 142 kW per rack denominator allocates the critical IT load across fully configured compute capacity, including each rack's pro rata share of external networking and storage power. The network, storage, and integration rows are cost allowances rather than additional power loads. Indented rows sum to total IT equipment.'

Indented sub-rows sum to the IT equipment row: 4.680 + 0.468 + 0.234 + 0.234 = 5.616; top-level rows sum to the total: 2.200 + 0.400 + 5.616 = 8.216. Share rounding: 26.8 + 4.9 + 68.4 = 100.1 and 57.0 + 5.7 + 2.8 + 2.8 = 68.3, both ≈ 100.0 / 68.4 due to rounding in the paper.
The $4.0m per-rack price 'already includes the GPUs, attached high-bandwidth memory, Grace CPUs, NVLink switching, power systems, and the physical rack' (Appendix A, PDF p.21).

Benchmark positioning (Appendix A, PDF p.20): $11m/MW facility benchmark is close to JLL (2026) $11.3m/MW and above Cleanview's $8.9m/MW average for 2025–26 completions; liquid cooling adds 7–10% (Turner & Townsend 2025). The $2m/MW power estimate is below Moody's implied $2.44m/MW (45 GW, $110B by 2030), so the paper calls it 'likely conservative'.

Footnote 10 (PDF p.21): rack count is a cluster-equivalent capacity measure — the 166.7 MW critical IT load is allocated across fully configured AI-compute capacity, not only GPU rack nameplate draw; network/storage/integration allowances are cost markups on the same unit, not additional power loads.

Table 2 indented sub-rows of IT equipment are carried structurally in the top-level `subrows` array, values verbatim: Integrated GB300 NVL72 systems [1,170 racks × $4.0m] = 4.68 $B (57.0%); External network fabric and fiber [10% of rack-system cost] = 0.468 $B (5.7%); Shared data storage [5% of rack-system cost] = 0.234 $B (2.8%); Integration and commissioning [5% of rack-system cost] = 0.234 $B (2.8%). They stay out of `rows` because the paper prints them indented under IT equipment — flat inclusion would double-count against the paper total 8.216 (sub-rows sum to the IT equipment row: 4.680 + 0.468 + 0.234 + 0.234 = 5.616).

rows hold the three top-level Table 2 lines together with the paper's Assumption column (added as the fourth view column); the four indented IT sub-rows (level=1, parent='IT equipment') are in `subrows`; the full-fidelity raw copy remains in data/raw/physical.json (campus_cost).
